pattern.title: Time and Work
pattern.description: Work efficiency, pipes and cisterns, and combined work problems.

questions.questionText: A can complete a work in 12 days and B in 18 days. In how many days can they complete it working together?
A can do a work in 20 days and B in 30 days. They work together for 5 days, then A leaves. In how many days will B complete the remaining work?
A pipe can fill a tank in 12 hours and another in 15 hours. Both pipes are opened together. How long will it take to fill the tank?
A can do a work in 8 days, B in 12 days, and C in 16 days. In how many days can they complete the work together?
A can complete a work in 10 days. B is 50% more efficient than A. In how many days can B complete the work alone?
Two pipes A and B can fill a tank in 8 hours and 12 hours respectively. A third pipe C can empty it in 6 hours. If all three are opened together, how long will it take to fill the tank?
A and B can do a piece of work in 18 days and 24 days respectively. They start together but B leaves after 6 days. In how many more days will A complete the remaining work?
A can do a work in 15 days and B in 20 days. They work together for 4 days, then A leaves. How long will B take to finish the remaining work?
A tap can fill a tank in 6 hours. After half the tank is filled, three more similar taps are opened. What is the total time taken to fill the tank completely?
questions.explanation: First half: 3 hours. Remaining half: rate = 4 taps, time = 3/4 = 0.75 hours = 45 min. Total = 3h 45m.

questions.questionText: A can do a work in 12 days, B in 18 days, and C in 24 days. In how many days can A, B, and C together complete the work?
A and B together can complete a work in 20 days. A alone can complete it in 30 days. In how many days can B alone complete the work?
A pipe can fill a tank in 10 hours. Due to a leak, it takes 15 hours to fill the tank. How long will the leak take to empty the full tank?
questions.explanation: Leak rate = 1/10 - 1/15 = 1/30. Time to empty = 30 hours.

questions.questionText: A can do a work in 16 days and B in 20 days. They work together for 5 days. What fraction of the work is completed?
A and B can complete a work in 12 days and 15 days respectively. A starts the work and works for 4 days, then B joins. In how many days will the remaining work be completed?
A can do a work in 25 days and B in 20 days. They work together for 5 days, then B leaves. How long will A take to finish the remaining work?
Three pipes A, B, and C can fill a tank in 6, 8, and 12 hours respectively. How long will they take to fill the tank together?
A can complete a work in 18 days, B in 24 days, and C in 36 days. In how many days can they complete it together?
A and B together can do a work in 10 days. A alone can do it in 15 days. In how many days can B alone do it?
A tap can fill a tank in 8 hours. A second tap can fill it in 12 hours. If both taps are opened together, how long will it take?
A can do a work in 9 days and B in 12 days. They start together but after 3 days, A leaves. How long will B take to finish the remaining work?
A pipe can fill a tank in 5 hours. Another pipe can empty it in 7 hours. If both are opened together, how long will it take to fill the tank?
A and B can complete a work in 6 days and 8 days respectively. They work together for 2 days, then B leaves. In how many days will A complete the remaining work?
A can do a work in 20 days and B in 30 days. They start together but A leaves after 6 days. In how many days will B complete the remaining work?
Two taps can fill a tank in 10 hours and 15 hours respectively. A third tap can empty it in 12 hours. If all are opened together, how long will it take to fill the tank?
A can complete a work in 14 days and B in 21 days. In how many days can they complete it working together?
